1947, January 10th
The following is a faithful transcription of the typed original by the Servant of God, Father Solarus Casey, O.F.M. Cap.
January 10th, 1947.
Mr. and Mrs. Joseph and Winifred O'Donnell 1120 Lake Drive Chicago, Ill.
Capuchin Franciscan Fathers Saint Felix Friary Huntington, Indiana.
My Dear Friends: God bless you and yours, - for brighter days and a more peaceful and successful new year, God willing.
I just received your letter of yesterday and am hoping to see you Monday night. Do not wory about coming late. It is very seldom I get on the matress till after 10 'clock.
Only last evening I wrote my Niece, Mrs. Dean Conley, of (I just have not the number) N.Riordan Road, that you were coming and asking them to get word to you I expected you. I invited them too. I want you tomeet them. I think you would enuoy eachother's company.
As for the Farm: Well, ofcourse such temporalities are always more or less a cause of worry what ever way one takes them. As you say: the times are so very upset and abnormal that it is no simple problem to carry on successfully at or with most any business. One hardly knows what to turn to or to invest in. I hoped from your letter a month or so ago - and I am sure you felt that way - that your visit to the S.West was providentially in your favor. I am inclined to confidence anyhow in Mr. Costello. Perhaps we ought to pray more for him and wait gently, viz, that he become a little more unselfish, etc. However, I was talking with Father Coughlin during that threatening Coal-stike about the general outlook and he wastelling us that the finantial-Jews seemed to be expecting a seriou depression, from the fact that at that time they were selling everything they could. Therefore, he concluded as did others, that they were figuring on something worse than came at least from that strike so far. I suppose that we can hardly do better than just pray on, doing the best we know from day today and trust in divine Providence with out too much anxiety. May the Good God guide us all!
I was just speaking to Father Guardian - our local Superior about inviting you and the Conleys and he too will be expecting you. He said: " .. We can acomodate seven guests nicely and fi necessary some of the men could be otherwise acomodated.
The Conleys have two little boys, the younger must bealittle over two years old. If you dont mind you could call them up to that effect.
INcidently, the old violin just arrived this p.m. and is in good condition. Thanks be to God for all His unsearchable designs.
Sincerely Yours in the SacredHeart,
I ought to say in the blessed Sacred Hearts of Jesus and Mary. Fr. Solanus, O.F.M. Cap Sinner.
